newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast Caistab reforms expected early 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast Caistab reforms expected early 1997.

text.p: Ivory Coast's new Caistab marketing board head, Yves-Marie Koissy, is expected to start reforms in early 1997, the government daily Fraternite Matin reported on Wednesday.

"The priorities of the new managing director are for the moment liberalisation and restructuring of the Caistab," the newspaper said. "He intends to bring in new roles for the Caistab which will bring about new work methods," it added.
Yves-Marie Koissy was speaking after a two-hour meeting with Ivorian President Henri Konan Bedie on Tuesday, but did not specify his plans, the paper said.
Former Caistab chief Rene Amany stepped down officially in October after 17 years at the head of Ivory Coast's powerful commodity marketing monopoly.
Industry sources expect Koissy, who arrived from his job at the International Monetary Fund in Washington, to push through market reforms to meet conditions for a $150 million World Bank loan.
Staff changes have begun, including replacement of the Casitab's cocoa department manager.
Industry sources expect early reforms to include revisions of a new automated produce auctioning system put in place in May to increase market efficiency and transparency.
A private report on coffee sector reforms for the World Bank is expected in January.
The Caistab has in the past set price levels across a broad spectrum of Ivory Coast's economy but its role, particularly in coffee and cocoa sectors, has been scaled down.
